literature.lead_zh: 本期SARS-CoV-2研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 库分析揭示了阶段特异性重塑,高亲和力结合抗体从 疫苗接种 后富含 IGHV1-46 的谱转变为感染后优先表达 IGHV3-30-3。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2751804]

news.headline_zh: SARS-CoV-2本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期SARS-CoV-2新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 该报告总结了 2026 年第 41 周期间英格兰的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2、流感和 RSV 的 监测 数据。它表明流感活动保持稳定并处于基线水平,而 RSV 活动增加并在基线水平循环。报告指出,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的活动呈现出混合趋势,且流通水平较低,确诊的急性呼吸道感染 (ARI) 事件数量稳定。 [news-536bef259f2c4ad3]
该文章报告了 CDC 对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的整体预测,这是正在进行的公共卫生监测和建模工作的一部分。它不描述已确认的 暴发 或事件。 [news-cd5805bb44a5390e]
A review article discusses the implications of COVID-19 vaccine boosters during pregnancy for protecting against preeclampsia, but no specific outbreak or event is reported. [news-41d0d2a5d7376c69]
Paxlovid, a promising antiviral pill for treating COVID-19, is in scarce supply, leading to competition among doctors and patients for access. [news-bb1c1497998ec7de]
里尔感染和免疫中心的研究人员在《科学报告》上发表的一项研究调查了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白 的 S1/S2 边界附近的 N 连接聚糖在 宿主 蛋白酶加工过程中的作用。研究结果表明,这些聚糖和补偿性碱性残基 (R634) 对于刺突切割和进入功能至关重要,并且它们的功能作用在不同变体中不断演变。 [news-0fcfcd4a5462b95e]

key_findings_en: The report summarizes the surveillance data for SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and RSV in England during week 41 of 2026. It indicates that influenza activity remained stable and at baseline levels, while RSV activity increased and was circulating at baseline levels. [news-536bef259f2c4ad3]

The article reports on the CDC's ensemble forecasts for SARS-CoV-2, which are part of ongoing public health monitoring and modeling efforts. It does not describe a confirmed outbreak or event. [news-cd5805bb44a5390e]
A review article discusses the implications of COVID-19 vaccine boosters during pregnancy for protecting against preeclampsia, but no specific outbreak or event is reported. [news-41d0d2a5d7376c69]

Paxlovid, a promising antiviral pill for treating COVID-19, is in scarce supply, leading to competition among doctors and patients for access. The drug was approved by federal regulators and began distribution in late 2021, but its availability remains limited, especially in certain states and counties. [news-bb1c1497998ec7de]

A study published in Scientific Reports by researchers at the Center for Infection and Immunity of Lille investigated the role of N-linked glycans near the S1/S2 boundary of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in its processing by host proteases. [news-0fcfcd4a5462b95e]

papers.title: Safety and immunogenicity of a first-generation modified vaccinia virus Ankara-vectored SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate with mRNA-based booster vaccination: A phase 1 trial
papers.abstract: The rapid development of effective COVID-19 vaccines was enabled by the parallel assessment of multiple candidates early in the pandemic, including candidates based on the Modified Vaccinia virus Ankara (MVA) vector platform. This Phase 1 trial (NCT04569383) evaluated the MVA-based vaccine candidate MVA-SARS-2-S, expressing the full-length native SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein (Wuhan-HU-1). Between October 2020 and May 2021, 30 healthy, SARS-CoV-2–naive adults received two doses of either 107 or 108 international units (IU) of MVA-SARS-2-S 28 days apart, with 6-month follow-up. A subgroup (n = 12) received two BNT162b2 booster vaccinations. Safety and reactogenicity were primary objectives; secondary and exploratory objectives included S1 seroconversion rates, S-domain-specific antibodies, SARS-CoV-2-neutralizing antibodies, and spike-specific T cell responses. MVA-SARS-2-S demonstrated a good safety profile. No severe or serious adverse events occurred. Immunogenicity was poor: S1-specific seroconversion occurred in 0/15 (107 IU group) and 3/15 (108 IU group) participants. Binding antibodies were predominantly directed against the S2 subunit, with peak median anti-S2 fold changes of 6.0 and 5.2 in the 107 IU and 108 IU groups, respectively. Neutralizing antibodies were detected in one participant (108 IU group); spike-specific T cell responses were observed in 5/15 (107 IU group) and 2/13 (108 IU group) participants. Heterologous BNT162b2 vaccination induced S1 seroconversion and detectable neutralizing antibody and T cell responses in all boosted participants, without safety concerns. In conclusion, while MVA-SARS-2-S was well tolerated and did not adversely affect subsequent BNT162b2 boosting, the vaccine candidate elicited insufficient immunogenicity, underscoring the need for optimized antigen design.

This Phase 1 trial (NCT04569383) evaluated the MVA-based vaccine candidate MVA-SARS-2-S, expressing the full-length native SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein (Wuhan-HU-1). MVA-SARS-2-S demonstrated a good safety profile. No severe or serious adverse events occurred. Immunogenicity was poor: S1-specific seroconversion occurred in 0/15 (107 IU group) and 3/15 (108 IU group) participants. Binding antibodies were predominantly directed against the S2 subunit, with peak median anti-S2 fold changes of 6.0 and 5.2 in the 107 IU and 108 IU groups, respectively. Neutralizing antibodies were detected in one participant (108 IU group); spike-specific T cell responses were observed in 5/15 (107 IU group) and 2/13 (108 IU group) participants. Heterologous BNT162b2 vaccination induced S1 seroconversion and detectable neutralizing antibody and T cell responses in all boosted participants, without safety concerns. In conclusion, while MVA-SARS-2-S was well tolerated and did not adversely affect subsequent BNT162b2 boosting, the vaccine candidate elicited insufficient immunogenicity, underscoring the need for optimized antigen design.

papers.title: The impact of COVID-19 vaccination on long COVID prevention in the Omicron era: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives To evaluate the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on the prevention of long COVID (LC) in the Omicron era through an updated systematic review and meta-analysis. Methods We performed an update of our previously published systematic review and meta-analysis of vaccination and LC risk (searches between 1 January 2022 and 1 March 2024). Databases (Embase, MEDLINE, PubMed, Europe PMC, LILACS, Cochrane COVID-19 Study Register) were searched for studies published between 1 March 2024 and 13 July 2026. Observational studies assessing the impact of vaccination on the risk of LC four or more weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection were included. Vaccines were restricted to those centrally authorised in the European Union. Random-effects meta-analyses, restricted to adults, were performed to calculate pooled odds ratios (OR) of LC in three comparisons: vaccinated (any dose) versus unvaccinated; booster vaccination versus unvaccinated; and booster vaccination versus primary course vaccination only. Results Nineteen new studies were identified, of which ten were included in the updated meta-analyses alongside eight studies from the original review. The pooled OR of LC in vaccinated adults (any dose) versus unvaccinated was 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67–0.84; 13 studies). ORs were also lower for booster vaccination versus unvaccinated (0.73; 95% CI 0.65–0.82; 6 studies), and booster vaccination versus primary course vaccination (0.63; 95% CI 0.53–0.75; 6 studies). Significant associations between vaccination and lower LC odds were observed in subgroup analyses of mRNA-only vaccination and LC outcomes three or more months after infection. Conclusions This updated review and meta-analysis reinforces our previous finding that vaccination may reduce the burden of LC in the Omicron era, with booster doses potentially providing additional protection. Although evidence in high-risk groups now prioritised for vaccination in most countries remains limited, these findings clearly demonstrate the benefits of vaccination and support current seasonal vaccination strategies.

papers.title: Telehealth-related education and training: a systematic review of recent developments since the COVID-19 pandemic
papers.abstract: The pandemic showed the potential of existing telehealth to increase healthcare access but also the need for healthcare workers to be competent and skilled in delivering care through this modality. We undertook a systematic literature review to identify telehealth-related courses developed since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and summarised study characteristics, learning objectives, and course content. Articles describing telehealth-related training and education programs implemented between 2020 and 2024 were included. Papers were required to list specific program content or learning objectives for any educational level or type of health professional. Two authors independently extracted data. Quality of articles was assessed against the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines. Quantitative data was summarised and reported using frequencies and percentages, learning objectives were mapped across the six Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) telehealth competency domains, and qualitative categories were thematically synthesised. Of 7547 articles identified, 51 were included. Most courses were implemented in the USA (82%), mostly targeted to undergraduate students (51%), and the number of articles per year increased over time. Most courses were developed by universities (53%), sometimes in collaboration with health services, and content was primarily applicable across multiple specialties. Participants nearly always evaluated the courses (90%). Content included basic knowledge and skills in telehealth, patient safety, and ethics, with learning objectives often on technology and communication. Only four programs included all AAMC telehealth competencies. This review highlights that telehealth education and training has expanded since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, however, current curricula are lacking experiential learning. Courses generally covered telehealth communication competencies in detail, but more content on the ethical and legal requirements, billing, physical examination, patient education, and eligibility for telehealth is required. For efficient resource use, standardised training can be applied across disciplines with addition of site or speciality-specific modules.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines the development of telehealth-related education and training programs since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. The review identified 51 articles describing such programs, primarily targeting undergraduate students in the USA. Most courses focused on basic telehealth knowledge, technology, and communication skills, but there was a notable lack of experiential learning and coverage of ethical, legal, billing, and eligibility aspects. papers.title: Longitudinal BCR repertoire dynamics reveal the evolution of broadly binding antibodies following heterologous SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and breakthrough infection: a single-donor case study
papers.abstract: Continued SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift and the persistent risk of zoonotic sarbecovirus spillover highlight the need for broadly protective countermeasures. Here, we longitudinally profiled the B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire of a single volunteer who received heterologous booster vaccination followed by Omicron BF.7 breakthrough infection, integrating bulk BCR sequencing with single B-cell culture and antibody binding analysis. Breakthrough infection was associated with broadened serum neutralization across SARS-CoV-2 variants and related sarbecoviruses, consistent with recall of antibodies targeting conserved epitopes. Repertoire analysis revealed stage-specific remodeling, with high-affinity binding antibodies shifting from an IGHV1-46-enriched profile after vaccination to preferential representation of IGHV3-30-3 after infection. Isolated monoclonal antibodies exhibited nanomolar-to-picomolar binding affinities to diverse animal-derived sarbecovirus spikes, with broad binding commonly, but not universally, associated with CDRH3 lengths of 14-16 amino acids. Phylogenetic and sequence analyses defined divergent evolutionary trajectories for IGHV1-46 and IGHV3-30-3 lineages, highlighting candidate genetic features that warrant validation in larger cohorts. Together, these findings describe how sequential heterologous antigen exposures can reshape the humoral repertoire in one individual and generate hypotheses for future pan-sarbecovirus antibody and vaccine studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the evolution of broadly neutralizing antibodies in a single donor following heterologous SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and Omicron BF.7 breakthrough infection. By analyzing the B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire through longitudinal profiling, the researchers observed shifts in antibody binding profiles, with high-affinity antibodies transitioning from an IGHV1-46-enriched state post-vaccination to a preferential IGHV3-30-3 representation after infection. The findings suggest that sequential antigen exposure can reshape the humoral immune response, offering insights into the development of broad-spectrum antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and related sarbecoviruses. The study highlights potential genetic features of antibodies that could be explored in larger cohorts for vaccine and therapeutic development. However, the results are based on a single donor, limiting generalizability and requiring further validation.

papers.abstract_zh: 持续的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 抗原漂移和人畜共患 sarbecovirus 跨物种溢出 的持续风险突出表明需要采取广泛的保护性对策。在这里,我们纵向分析了接受异源加强 疫苗接种 后接受 Omicron BF.7 突破性感染的单个志愿者的 B 细胞受体 (BCR) 库,将批量 BCR 测序与单个 B 细胞培养和抗体结合分析相结合。突破性感染与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体和相关 sarbecovirus 的血清中和作用扩大有关,这与针对保守表位的抗体的回忆一致。库分析揭示了阶段特异性重塑,高亲和力结合抗体从 疫苗接种 后富含 IGHV1-46 的谱转变为感染后优先表达 IGHV3-30-3。分离的单克隆抗体对多种动物源性 sarbecovirus 刺突表现出纳摩尔至皮摩尔的结合亲和力,通常具有广泛的结合,但并非普遍如此,与 14-16 个氨基酸的 CDRH3 长度相关。系统发育和序列分析定义了 IGHV1-46 和 IGHV3-30-3 谱系的不同进化轨迹,突出了需要在更大的 队列研究 中进行验证的候选遗传特征。总之,这些发现描述了连续的异源抗原暴露如何重塑个体的体液库,并为未来的泛沙病毒抗体和 疫苗 研究提供假设。

papers.title: Protection of Omicron XBB.1.5 vaccine, previous infection, and their induced neutralizing antibodies against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection during Omicron KP.3 wave
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Data are limited on the protection of Omicron XBB.1.5 vaccine, previous infection, and their induced neutralizing antibodies against Omicron KP.3 infection. METHODS: Among 1826 tertiary hospital staff in Tokyo who had received three or more doses of COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and provided blood samples in June 2024, we prospectively examined the associations of XBB.1.5 vaccination and previous infection (classified by the timing of the last infection as pre-Omicron XBB, Omicron XBB, or Omicron JN.1 waves) with the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron KP.3 wave (June to September 2024). In a nested case-control analysis, we compared pre-infection live-virus KP.3.3-neutralizing antibody titers between cases and 1: 1 propensity-score matched controls. RESULTS: XBB.1.5 vaccination was not associated with measurable protection against symptomatic infection (4%, 95% CI, -88 to 51). Previous infection conferred protection that increased with its recency: 26% (95% CI, -26 to 56) for pre-Omicron XBB, 44% (95% CI, 2 to 68) for Omicron XBB, and 89% (95% CI, 52 to 97) for Omicron JN.1 waves. Pre-infection KP.3.3-neutralizing titers tended to be lower in cases than in matched controls (GMT ratio 0.68, 95% CI, 0.35 to 1.33); KP.3.3-neutralizing activity was only modestly elevated by XBB.1.5 vaccination but markedly higher after recent JN.1 infection. CONCLUSIONS: During the Omicron KP.3 wave, when an updated vaccine was unavailable, XBB.1.5 vaccination administered approximately 7 months earlier conferred no measurable neutralizing activity or protection against symptomatic KP.3 infection. Previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly recent JN.1-wave infection, affords substantial neutralizing titers and protection.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the protective efficacy of the Omicron XBB.1.5 vaccine and previous SARS-CoV-2 infection against symptomatic Omicron KP.3 infection during the KP.3 wave in Tokyo. Among 1826 tertiary hospital staff who had received three or more doses of mRNA vaccines, the study found that XBB.1.5 vaccination did not provide measurable protection against KP.3 infection. In contrast, previous infection conferred protection, with the highest level observed for recent JN.1-wave infections. The study used a nested case-control design, comparing neutralizing antibody titers between cases and matched controls. The findings suggest that natural immunity from recent infections may offer stronger protection than vaccination against emerging variants. However, the study's results are limited by the lack of an updated vaccine during the KP.3 wave, and the evidence for vaccine efficacy is weak. These results have implications for understanding the role of vaccination and natural immunity in protecting against new variants of SARS-CoV-2.

papers.title: Evaluation of pre-Omicron population immunity for SARS-CoV-2 in the Household Influenza Vaccine Evaluation (HIVE) cohort
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Continued serosurvey for SARS-CoV-2 population immunity is critical for vaccine strain selection and identification of susceptible groups such as young children. We aim to evaluate the use of a high-throughput, low-volume assay to describe strain-specific IgG measurement in a longitudinally followed community based cohort. METHODS: The longitudinal Household Influenza Vaccine Evaluation study has observed around 300 households annually for acute respiratory illness. SARS-CoV-2 variant-specific IgG (including original, Delta, Beta, and Omicron variants) concentrations were measured using multiplex electrochemiluminescence (ECL), pseudoviral neutralization (PN), and ACE2 inhibition assays in participants who had serum samples drawn between July 1 and December 31, 2021. Spearman's rank correlation coefficient assessed correlation within and between ECL, ACE2, and PN assays. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated the performance of ECL and ACE2 assays. Generalized additive mixed models estimated population immunity by age against SARS-CoV-2 variants. RESULTS: A total of 156 serum samples from 117 participants were selected for this study. Most (65.8%) were from adults and a majority (77.8%) received vaccination during the analysis period. High correlations were observed within ECL IgG assays (0.95-1.00), within ACE2 inhibition assays (0.70-0.99), and between assay platforms, including ECL versus PN (0.81-0.83) and ACE2 versus PN (0.88-0.95). SARS-CoV-2 IgG concentrations generally increased with age and appeared to plateau in early adulthood, although estimates were imprecise in younger age groups because of small sample sizes. CONCLUSION: We found a high correlation between ECL, ACE2, and PN across variants. Age-specific IgG quantities reflected behavior and infection histories collected by active surveillance.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 持续进行 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 群体免疫血清调查对于 疫苗 菌株选择和易感群体(例如幼儿)的鉴定至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们的目标是评估使用高通量、低容量测定来描述基于 队列研究 的纵向跟踪社区中的菌株特异性 IgG 测量。
elements_zh.methods: 纵向家庭流感 疫苗 评估研究每年观察约 300 个家庭是否患有急性呼吸道疾病。使用多重电化学发光 (ECL)、伪病毒中和 (PN) 和 ACE2 抑制测定对 2021 年 7 月 1 日至 12 月 31 日期间抽取血清样本的参与者测量 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体特异性 IgG(包括原始、Delta、Beta 和 Omicron 变体)浓度。在 ECL IgG 测定 (0.95-1.00) 和 ACE2 抑制测定中观察到高度相关性(0.70-0.99),以及检测平台之间的比较,包括 ECL 与 PN (0.81-0.83) 以及 ACE2 与 PN (0.88-0.95)。
elements_zh.main_results: 本研究共选取了 117 名参与者的 156 份血清样本。严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 IgG 浓度通常随着年龄的增长而增加,并在成年早期趋于稳定,但由于样本量较小,在较年轻的年龄组中的估计值并不精确。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们发现不同变体的 ECL、ACE2 和 PN 之间存在高度相关性。年龄特异性 IgG 数量反映了活跃的 监测 收集的行为和感染史。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为疫苗毒株的选择以及识别易感群体(特别是年轻儿童)提供信息,从而了解人群对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株的免疫应答情况。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究设计的局限性包括较年轻年龄组的样本量较小,这可能会影响年龄特异性 IgG 估计的精确度。证据强度中等。

RESULTS: A total of 156 serum samples from 117 participants were selected for this study. Most (65.8%) were from adults and a majority (77.8%) received vaccination during the analysis period. High correlations were observed within ECL IgG assays (0.95-1.00), within ACE2 inhibition assays (0.70-0.99), and between assay platforms, including ECL versus PN (0.81-0.83) and ACE2 versus PN (0.88-0.95). SARS-CoV-2 IgG concentrations generally increased with age and appeared to plateau in early adulthood, although estimates were imprecise in younger age groups because of small sample sizes. CONCLUSION: We found a high correlation between ECL, ACE2, and PN across variants. Age-specific IgG quantities reflected behavior and infection histories collected by active surveillance.

papers.title: Genomic surveillance of COVID-19 in Hong Kong (2020-2023): Analysing SARS-CoV-2 variants, mutations, and their impact on viral entry.
papers.abstract: Abstract We analysed 15,982 quality-controlled SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences from Hong Kong, obtained from NCBI and GISAID between 2020 and 2023, to characterize lineage dynamics, mutational profiles, demographic distributions, and variant-specific viral entry. Genomic surveillance identified 543 lineages and 5,982 unique mutations. Lineages A, B, and B.4 dominated the initial epidemic waves, whereas Delta and Omicron emerged and predominated in later waves. Omicron BA.1 and BA.2 exhibited distinct distributions across gender and age groups, while JN.1 harboured several novel mutations. Molecular simulations comparing spike receptor-binding domain (SRBD)–ACE2 interactions revealed significant differences in binding affinity among variants (F = 4.404, p = 9.12 × 10−7). JN.1 demonstrated enhanced ACE2-binding affinity, suggesting increased viral entry and potential transmissibility. By integrating genomic, demographic, and molecular evidence, this study provides a comprehensive account of SARS-CoV-2 evolution in Hong Kong and highlights the public health relevance of emerging variants. These findings support sustained genomic surveillance and demographic monitoring to strengthen pandemic preparedness. Future research should evaluate public health strategies and adopt holistic frameworks integrating population characteristics with genomic evidence to mitigate the effects of future variants.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein hijacks host transcription by targeting eEF1A1
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 variants display substantial genetic and phenotypic diversity, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying their effects on host gene regulation need further investigation. We performed a transcriptomic analysis of host responses to multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta and Omicron. Despite their divergence, all variants induced a conserved transcriptional program in human lung epithelial cells characterized by activation of interferon regulatory factors (IRFs), immediate–early genes, and downstream cytokines. We identify the viral nucleocapsid (N) protein as a central driver of this transcriptional reprogramming, as N expression alone partially recapitulated the host response to infection. Mechanistically, N promotes recruitment of interferon regulatory factors and AP-1 transcription factors, RNA polymerase II, and the elongation factor eEF1A1 to promoters of pro-inflammatory genes, revealing a previously unrecognized nuclear role for eEF1A1. Disruption of the N-eEF1A1 interaction, genetically or pharmacologically using the eEF1A interactant plitidepsin, abolished transcriptional complex formation and reversed host gene dysregulation, identifying a conserved host–virus regulatory axis and potential pan-variant therapeutic target.

papers.title: A Genome-Wide Association Study in the Chilean admixed population reveals four new loci for COVID-19 severity and susceptibility
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background More than five years after the COVID-19 outbreak, the infection by the SARS-CoV-2 virus should still be considered as a global threat with highly heterogeneous clinical outcomes from asymptomatic to fatal depending on existing genetic and phenotypic inter-individual and inter-population variability. Our objective is to identify risk loci associated with COVID-19 in an admixed Latin American population. Methods We performed a genome-wide association study in the framework of the Chilean C19-GenoNet team, analyzing a cohort of 3,417 individuals recruited from the northernmost to the southernmost regions of the country, who presented variations in the severity of their COVID-19 clinical manifestations. Results Our investigation replicated the extensively reported association of several variants at the 3p21.31 locus with COVID-19 severity and found a suggestive association for a variant within the FOXP4 gene at 6p21.1 with COVID-19 hospitalization. Both associations appear to be shared with other populations. Importantly, our study identified three previously unreported loci associated with COVID-19 severity or hospitalization at 7q21.11, 16p13.12 and 6p25.3, and one additional locus at 4p13 associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity, a proxy for infection susceptibility. Conclusions these new risk loci may represent population-specific effects in Chilean and, potentially, other Latin American admixed groups. Our study highlights the importance of expanding efforts to study underrepresented and genetically different populations, which may provide new clues on the genetic basis of human diseases and may help to anticipate global responses to emerging viral infections and future pandemics.

papers.title: Germinal center dynamics in the mediastinal lymph node distinguish time-dependent and variant-specific immunity during SARS-CoV-2 secondary exposure
papers.abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 secondary infections remain a persistent challenge even though individuals have previous immunity from natural infection or vaccination. Yet, the cellular mechanisms that determine whether a secondary exposure is rapidly controlled by pre-existing immunity and results in sterilizing protection or progresses to productive infection and disease remain poorly understood. Using homologous and heterologous secondary-challenge experimental strategies in C57BL/6J mice, we show that protection against a homologous SARS-CoV-2 Alpha secondary challenge in previously infected mice is time-limited, remaining durable through 56 days post-primary infection, with breakthrough infection on day 84 post-primary infection. This loss of protection was not associated with waning neutralizing antibody titers but instead correlated with progressive contraction of T follicular helper cells and germinal center B cells in the mediastinal lymph node. In contrast, heterologous Beta secondary exposure in Alpha-previously infected mice consistently failed to mount a robust germinal center response despite mobilizing comparable or greater numbers of immune cells than homologous re-challenge. Instead, RNA-seq and flow cytometry analyses revealed that this response was associated with an inflammatory extrafollicular B cell response characterized by reduced Bcl6 and Aicda expression and concomitant robust upregulation of Il6 . Taken together, these findings identify the germinal center recall response in the mediastinal lymph node as an important cellular correlate of SARS-CoV-2 secondary immunity and carry direct implications for the timing of booster immunization and the design of cross-variant vaccines.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用 C57BL/6J 小鼠进行同源和异源二次攻击实验,以研究 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 免疫。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究在 C57BL/6J 小鼠中采用同源和异源二次攻击实验策略,利用 RNA-seq 和流式细胞术分析来评估 免疫应答。
elements_zh.main_results: 针对同源 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Alpha 二次攻击的保护是有时间限制的,突破性感染发生在初次感染后第 84 天。先前感染 Alpha 的小鼠中,异源 Beta 二次暴露并未引起强烈的生发中心反应,而是表现出炎症性滤泡外 B 细胞反应。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果受到动物模型的使用和所使用的特定小鼠品系的限制,可能无法完全推广到人类群体。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要:即使个体先前对自然感染或 疫苗接种 具有免疫力,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 继发感染仍然是一个持续的挑战。然而,对于决定二次暴露是否受到预先存在的免疫力快速控制并导致消毒保护或进展为生产性感染和疾病的细胞机制仍知之甚少。在 C57BL/6J 小鼠中使用同源和异源二次攻击实验策略,我们表明,对先前感染的小鼠的同源 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Alpha 二次攻击的保护是有时间限制的,在初次感染后 56 天保持持久,在初次感染后第 84 天突破感染。这种保护的丧失与中和抗体滴度的减弱无关,而是与纵隔淋巴结中滤泡辅助T细胞和生发中心B细胞的进行性收缩相关。相比之下,先前感染α的小鼠中的异源β二次暴露始终未能产生强有力的生发中心反应,尽管与同源再次攻击相比动员了相当或更多数量的免疫细胞。相反,RNA-seq 和流式细胞术分析表明,这种反应与滤泡外 B 细胞炎症反应相关,其特征是 Bcl6 和 Aicda 表达减少,同时 Il6 强烈上调。总而言之,这些发现确定纵隔淋巴结中的生发中心回忆反应是 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 二次免疫的重要细胞相关性,并对加强免疫的时机和交叉变体 疫苗 的设计具有直接影响。

papers.title: Vaccination and Non-School NPIs Shaped Ontario's Pre-Omicron COVID-19 Hospital Burden
papers.abstract: We develop an age- and immunity-structured COVID-19 model with setting-specific contacts, calibrated to Ontario incidence and hospital admissions before Omicron. We simulate counterfactual vaccination strategies and contact restrictions in schools, workplaces, and other community settings, evaluating projected severe-case demand against an illustrative healthcare-capacity benchmark. Vaccination combined with workplace and community contact restrictions keeps simulated demand within capacity. In contrast, relaxing restrictions in either setting produces large surges and repeated capacity threats, even when school restrictions remain. School-only changes produce smaller effects on severe disease. These findings highlight the value of vaccination and setting-specific contact restrictions that prioritize workplace and community settings for pathogens with adult-concentrated severe outcomes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate how vaccination and non-school non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) influenced the hospital burden of COVID-19 in Ontario before the Omicron variant emerged, addressing the need to understand the impact of these measures on severe disease outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a counterfactual simulation approach to model the effects of different vaccination strategies and contact restrictions in workplaces and community settings, alongside school restrictions, on the projected demand for hospital beds in Ontario during the pre-Omicron period.
analysis.methods: The researchers developed an age- and immunity-structured model calibrated to Ontario's incidence and hospital admission data, simulating various scenarios of vaccination and contact restrictions to assess their impact on severe-case demand.
analysis.main_results: Relaxing contact restrictions in workplaces or community settings led to large surges in severe-case demand, even when school restrictions remained in place. School-only changes had smaller effects on severe disease outcomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that combining vaccination with targeted contact restrictions in adult-dominated settings is more effective in managing hospital demand than relying solely on school-based interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform public health strategies by emphasizing the importance of prioritizing workplace and community contact restrictions alongside vaccination to mitigate severe outcomes of SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on simulated data and does not account for real-world variability, which may limit the generalizability of its findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the model-based nature of the analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the impact of vaccination and non-school non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) on the hospital burden of pre-Omicron SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario. Using a counterfactual simulation model, the researchers assess how varying levels of vaccination and contact restrictions in workplaces and community settings affect severe-case demand. They find that relaxing restrictions in these adult-concentrated environments leads to significant surges in hospital demand, even with school restrictions in place. In contrast, school-only changes have smaller effects on severe disease outcomes. The study highlights the importance of prioritizing workplace and community-based NPIs in conjunction with vaccination to manage hospital capacity. However, the reliance on simulated data introduces limitations, reducing the strength of the evidence to moderate.

papers.title: Fitness flux in SARS-CoV-2 and influenza H3N2
papers.abstract: The tempo of viral adaptation is usually read indirectly from the composition of mutations, through measures such as dN/dS. Here we measure it directly from the dynamics of variant frequencies, where we use multinomial logistic regression to estimate a fitness for each co-circulating variant. We aggregate these estimates to derive the rate of change of mean population fitness, referred to as fitness flux. Tracing SARS-CoV-2 from its emergence, we find that it initially adapted rapidly, doubling in fitness every 6 months from Jan 2021 to Jun 2022, but slowing to every 2.4 years from Jul 2022 to Dec 2025. Seasonal influenza H3N2 sustained a slower, steadier pace doubling in fitness every 10.0 years. In both, the rate of fitness gain closely tracks the variance in fitness, matching the 1:1 expectation of Fisher’s fundamental theorem. Phylogenetic contrasts between parent and child lineages localize most fitness gain to spike, and within spike to the receptor-binding domain, where a simple count of spike S1 substitutions predicts lineage fitness about as well as deep-learning escape and protein-language-model scores. Measuring fitness directly thus offers a transparent, frequency-based alternative to mutational proxies for tracking and anticipating viral adaptation. The website blab.github.io/fitness-flux/ is the intended reading experience of this paper, providing responsive layout and interactive figures.

papers.title: Global burden of type 2 diabetes attributable to SARS-CoV-2 infection
papers.abstract: Objective We aimed to quantify the association between severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and the risk of incident diabetes. We also aimed to estimate the global burden of incident type 2 diabetes (T2D) attributable to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies identified through PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and CENTRAL from inception to 29 January 2026. analysis.summary_en: This review quantifies the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and the risk of incident type 2 diabetes (T2D). A systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 cohort studies involving 48.9 million participants found a modest increased risk of T2D following SARS-CoV-2 infection (pooled RR, 1.25 [95% CI, 1.16–1.34]), although heterogeneity and a 95% prediction interval that included the null suggest uncertainty. papers.title: Pathophysiology of Lung Cancer in the Context of SARS-CoV-2 Variants of Concern
papers.abstract: Many retrospective cohort studies have revealed that patients with cancer are at increased risk of severe complications and mortality from COVID-19 due to a multitude of factors, including advanced age in this cohort, high incidence of underlying comorbidities, and immunosuppression caused by cancer and its treatments. It has been futher demonstrated that individuals with lung cancer face a disproportionately higher risk of mortality compared to other cancer types following SARS-SoV-2 infection. However, several questions remain unanswered regarding the understanding of the pathophysiology of lung cancer in the context of COVID-19, as well as the effects of SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern on patient outcomes. The article aims to investigate the following gaps the clinical manifestation of SARS-CoV-2 infection in patients with lung cancer: the molecular characteristics of lung cancer driving the development of severe COVID-19, and the role of COVID-19-induced inflammation in accelerating the development and increasing the severity of lung cancer, particularly with respect to the Alpha (B.1.1.7), Beta (B.1.351), Gamma (P.1) and Delta (B.1.617.2) variants. Understanding the crosstalk between lung cancer and COVID-19, particularly concerning the early variants of concern, will reveal the unique mechanisms contributing to poor outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 in patients with lung cancer, including the maintenance of a hyperinflammatory state, TMPRSS2 expression patterns, and tumor-associated immune evasion, among others. This work will be valuable in the development of improved antivirals and vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 in the cancer population and will help provide insight into the pathogenesis of current and emerging variants of concern in this at-risk cohort. Additional studies and a high degree of caution are essential in understanding the impacts of newer and emerging variants of concern such as Omicron (B.1.1.529) and its subvariants on patients with lung cancer.

papers.title: Informing risk stratification and vaccine policy via a predictive mathematical model of SARS-COV-2 infection
papers.abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 human challenge studies enabled unprecedented high frequency temporal measurements of immune determinants of viral control. We integrated prior knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 replication, innate, cytotoxic T cell and antibody responses into a dynamic model which captured viral-load kinetics in seronegative volunteers challenged with wildtype virus. The model predicted measured innate and adaptive immune dynamics. Perturbation analyses indicated that innate immunity limits peak viral load, whereas antibodies principally mediate clearance while cytotoxic T cells become critical in antibody deficiency. Pre-existing antibodies suppressed both viral replication and subsequent immune activation- a prediction validated in a second challenge study of seropositive participants infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. The model explains how specific immunodeficiencies may increase susceptibility to severe or persistent infection, supporting clinical risk stratification. It suggests that T cell-targeted vaccination strategies may provide limited protection without effective neutralising antibodies, and that attenuated boosting after low-dose exposure requires repeated vaccination to reduce breakthrough infections, informing public health policy. One Sentence Summary A mathematical model of SARS-COV-2 infection predicts innate and adaptive immunity, and informs risk stratification and vaccine policy.

papers.title: Immune parameters in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during SARS-CoV2 delta and omicron waves.
papers.abstract: Understanding immune mechanisms associated with COVID-19 severity remains important for interpreting clinical outcomes. We investigated virological and immunological profiles in 39-patients hospitalized with COVID-19 at InCor Hospital during the Delta and Omicron waves and included 28-non-hospitalized individuals with moderate COVID-19 as a comparator group for cytokine analyses. SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed by RT-PCR from nasopharyngeal swabs, and viral variants were identified by next-generation sequencing. RNAemia was assessed by RT-PCR and analyzed as a binary variable. Serum cytokines were quantified by cytometric bead array, while humoral responses were evaluated by anti-Spike RBD IgG levels using CLIA and a Wuhan-Hu-1-based pseudovirus neutralization assay. RNAemia was more frequent in ICU-admitted patients than in non-ICU patients, supporting an association with disease severity. Cytokine profiling showed increased IL-6, IL-8, TNF, IL-17 A and IL-10 levels in hospitalized patients compared with moderate COVID-19 individuals, but did not distinguish recovered from deceased patients. Neutralizing antibody titers measured against a Wuhan-Hu-1 spike pseudovirus were significantly higher in recovered individuals than decease patients, underscoring the relevance of antibody functionality. These data emphasize the relevance of viral dissemination and functional humoral immunity as potential biomarkers for COVID-19 progression and outcome, with RNAemia and neutralizing antibody levels showing a stronger exploratory association in this cohort.

papers.title: Impact of Community Factors on Mental and Physical Health During Successive Waves of COVID-19 Pandemic in China.
papers.abstract: This study examined how community factors impacted well-being during the COVID-19 pandemic in China. Data were collected at two time points: Time 1 (T1) in September 2021 (N = 992) when COVID-19 cases stabilized, and Time 2 (T2) in January 2023 (N = 497) during a sudden outbreak of new infected cases. At T1, perceived community safety and sense of community directly affected depression, anxiety, and physical health symptoms, with sense of community partially mediating these effects. At T2, community factors at T1 continued to impact depression, anxiety, and physical health symptoms. Sense of community at T1 partially mediated the link between community safety at T1 and mental health at T2. Higher income and older age were associated with a stronger sense of community, better perceived community safety, and improved health. Policymakers should consider the impact of community factors on well-being during health crises.

papers.title: Association between COVID-19 vaccination, SARS-CoV-2 infection, and oral lichen planus (OLP) flares: Results from a patient survey
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic immune-mediated mucocutaneous disease. During the COVID-19 pandemic, new cases and flares of OLP were reported after SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination. Immune activation and cytokine release triggered by infection or vaccines are proposed mechanisms, although current evidence is limited. Clarifying this relationship is important for improving patient counseling and management during vaccination efforts. OBJECTIVES: The study aimed to explore the association with an increased occurrence of OLP flares following COVID-19 vaccination or infection. MATERIAL AND METHODS: An 11-question survey was distributed to OLP patients. The questionnaire aimed to inquire about the history of COVID-19 vaccination and infection as it related to subjective flares of OLP (oral redness, ulcerations, pain, or discomfort). Associations with complications were assessed with Fisher's exact or Wilcoxon tests. RESULTS: Seventy-six patients participated in the survey. Twenty percent of study participants reported experiencing a flare after COVID-19 vaccination (n = 13), and 33% after an infection (n = 13). Self-reported OLP flares were significantly associated with whether or not participants also reported vaccine side effects (p = 0.005). Among the 27 participants who reported experiencing systemic post-vaccination side effects (tiredness, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, nausea), 37% (n = 10) also reported an OLP flare compared with 8% (n = 3) of the 38 who did not report systemic side effects from the COVID-19 vaccination. Of the 63 participants who received a 2nd vaccine dose, 21% (n = 13) reported experiencing an OLP flare. Experiencing systemic side effects following the 2nd vaccination was again significantly associated with reporting an OLP flare (p = 0.048). CONCLUSIONS: Overall, OLP flares were not reported at high rates with COVID-19 vaccination or infection. Within these limitations, the findings of the study suggest that participants who experience systemic side effects following a COVID-19 vaccine may be more susceptible to OLP flares. Experiencing an OLP flare following the 1st COVID-19 vaccination was significantly associated with experiencing a flare again after receiving the 2nd vaccination.
papers.journal: Advances in Clinical and Experimental Medicine

Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic immune-mediated mucocutaneous disease. During the COVID-19 pandemic, new cases and flares of OLP were reported after SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: An 11-question survey was distributed to OLP patients. Associations with complications were assessed with Fisher's exact or Wilcoxon tests.

analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study reports that self-reported OLP flares were significantly associated with whether or not participants also reported vaccine side effects (p = 0.005). However, the evidence is limited and based on self-reporting, which may introduce bias. The study also found that experiencing systemic side effects following the 2nd vaccination was again significantly associated with reporting an OLP flare (p = 0.048).
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Clarifying this relationship is important for improving patient counseling and management during vaccination efforts. Experiencing an OLP flare following the 1st COVID-19 vaccination was significantly associated with experiencing a flare again after receiving the 2nd vaccination.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination and oral lichen planus (OLP) flares through a survey of 76 OLP patients. It reports that 20% of participants experienced OLP flares after vaccination, and 33% after infection. Self-reported OLP flares were significantly linked to vaccine side effects (p = 0.005), with 37% of those reporting systemic side effects also experiencing flares compared to 8% without side effects. A second dose of the vaccine was associated with 21% of participants reporting flares. The study concludes that OLP flares are not commonly reported with vaccination or infection, but those experiencing systemic side effects may be more susceptible. The findings highlight the need for improved patient counseling and management during vaccination efforts, and suggest further research into the relationship between vaccine-induced immune responses and OLP flares.

papers.title: Severity-dependent and sex-biased dysregulation of A-to-I RNA editing in COVID-19 reveals CTSS as a key regulatory target
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT SARS-CoV-2 infection causes diverse clinical outcomes, with men facing higher risks of severe disease. Adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing mediated by ADAR enzymes governs innate antiviral immunity, yet its contribution to COVID-19 severity and sex-biased disease remains unclear. We performed epitranscriptomic profiling on 126 blood samples from non-COVID controls and COVID-19 patients spanning different disease severities. We detected 1,466 differentially RNA-edited sites in 514 genes linked to clinical outcomes. Although ADAR expression increased in COVID-19 patients overall, it was strongly reduced in ICU patients compared with non-ICU patients, and this shift was far more prominent in males. This severity-associated and sex-biased ADAR/ADARB1 downregulation coincided with decreased global RNA editing and perturbed expression of immune-related edited transcripts. Cathepsin S (CTSS) was identified as a central regulatory node: elevated A-to-I editing within its 3’ UTR in ICU patients stabilizes CTSS mRNA. Without stratifying by disease severity, ADAR expression and global editing showed no significant sex differences; the large sex divergence only appeared among ICU patients. This indicates severity-dependent, not infection-innate, disruption of A-to-I editing, disproportionately amplified in critically ill males. CTSS 3’UTR editing may serve as a biomarker for patient stratification, revealing a mechanistic connection between epitranscriptomic changes and male-biased severe COVID-19.

papers.title: Administrative Primacy as an Interpretive Framework for Health System Governance: A Document-Based Analysis of Three Publicly Reported Episodes During the 2021 Fujian COVID-19 Outbreak Response
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Public health emergencies can intensify ethical risks rather than suspend them. When emergency governance is structured primarily around administrative performance metrics, established clinical and occupational protection norms may face displacement pressure. This case study examines three publicly reported episodes from the 2021 Fujian Delta variant COVID-19 outbreak through the interpretive lens of Administrative Primacy, a descriptive framework for analysing governance patterns in which administrative performance objectives may structurally outweigh clinical judgment and ethical reasoning. Administrative Primacy is introduced here as a sensitising concept rather than a formal theory, analogous to interpretive constructs used in governance and organisational ethics research. Methods We conducted a document-based ethical case analysis using exclusively publicly available sources: official government communications, state-approved media reports, and peer-reviewed literature. All cited documentary sources are publicly accessible and independently retrievable. Ethical interpretation was informed, where applicable, by selected principles of the Declaration of Helsinki (2013), supplemented by WHO outbreak-ethics guidance, NHC pediatric imaging standards (WS 521–2017), and UV radiation safety regulations (GB 19258 − 2012). A Poisson incidence density model was applied as an auxiliary sensitivity analysis to examine the plausibility of a reported occupational outcome; full derivation and sensitivity analyses are in Supplementary Methods S1. Evidence is categorised by type throughout: official photographs, official regulatory text, official press conference records, and state-approved media reports are distinguished from interpretive inference. Results Three domains of concern were identified, each supported by publicly accessible documentary sources, including official documents and contemporaneous media reports. First, a state-media-documented pediatric CT episode involved the simultaneous co-occurrence of three concurrent ethical and regulatory concerns: an unaccompanied minor in a radiological environment (contrary to WS 521–2017), an apparently illuminated UV germicidal lamp during the child’s presence (which would be contrary to GB 19258 − 2012 if operating as depicted), and CT application to a cohort characterised by the NHC’s own lead expert as predominantly mild. Second, the overnight mobilisation of 320 pre-licensure medical students for 27 days of high-frequency nasopharyngeal sampling raised occupational safety and consent concerns; auxiliary Poisson analysis suggested the reported zero-infection outcome was lower than would be anticipated under the stated comparator assumptions, raising a question that warrants verification. Third, a ‘Green Channel’ administrative exception at the region’s designated tertiary hospital temporally associated with a sequence of events culminating in ICU closure, creating structural conditions that may have been associated with delayed critical care access; no mortality estimate is made. Conclusions The three episodes are consistent with, and may be interpreted through, the Administrative Primacy framework as illustrations of a governance pattern in which administrative performance metrics may, in some circumstances, come into tension with clinical ethics, occupational protection norms, and institutional transparency. The framework is offered as a replicable analytical tool for evaluating governance-ethics alignment in future emergency responses, and three domains are identified as candidate areas for further health-system governance review, framed as hypotheses generated by this single case rather than as established broader policy gaps.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the 2021 Fujian Delta variant outbreak of SARS-CoV-2 through the lens of Administrative Primacy, a framework highlighting how administrative performance metrics may influence clinical judgment and ethical reasoning. Three episodes are analyzed: a pediatric CT case involving regulatory and ethical concerns, the mobilization of medical students for sampling with safety and consent issues, and a hospital administrative exception linked to ICU closure. The review identifies these as potential illustrations of governance patterns where administrative priorities may conflict with clinical ethics and occupational norms. While the framework is presented as a hypothesis for future governance review, the study underscores the need for verification of reported outcomes and the importance of aligning administrative practices with ethical standards during public health emergencies.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的2021年福建三角洲变体暴发的治理,研究行政绩效指标如何影响突发公共卫生事件期间的临床判断和道德推理。核心问题是,行政至上是否可以被视为此类危机期间卫生系统治理的一种模式。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查采用基于文档的道德案例分析,使用公开来源:官方政府通讯、国家批准的媒体报道和同行评审的文献。使用泊松 发病率 密度模型作为辅助敏感性分析来评估报告的职业结果的合理性。所有引用的文献来源均可公开访问且可独立检索。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 确定了三个值得关注的领域,每个领域都有文献资料支持,包括官方文件和媒体报道。这些事件与行政首要框架一致,该框架表明,在某些情况下,行政绩效指标可能与临床伦理、职业保护规范和机构透明度相冲突。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 连夜动员 320 名预执照医学生进行高频鼻咽采样,引发了职业安全和同意方面的担忧。报告的零感染结果低于比较假设下的预期,因此需要进行验证。此外,该框架是作为假设而不是既定的政策差距提出的。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该框架作为可复制的分析工具提供,用于评估未来应急响应中的治理与道德一致性。三个领域被确定为进一步卫生系统治理审查的候选领域,并以此单一案例产生的假设为框架。

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Live Attenuated COVID-19 Vaccine Candidate Based on Omicron-like Temperature-Sensitive Mutant in Preclinical Study
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has ended, emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants remain a future threat. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of an intranasal live attenuated vaccine (LAV) prototype based on a temperature-sensitive (ts) Omicron-like SARS-CoV-2 mutant in a Syrian hamster COVID-19 model. Methods: SARS-CoV-2 Dubrovka (Wuhan-like), Otradnoe (BA.1.1) and FEB2 (BA.5.2) strains and the ts F-F3 mutant derived from FEB2 were characterized by electron microscopy, nanopore sequencing, cytopathic effect titration, and RT-PCR. In vitro studies used Vero CCL-81 cells; in vivo transmissibility and efficacy studies were assessed in female Syrian hamsters. Serum antibody titers were measured by ELISA and neutralization assays. Immunization efficacy was assessed by weight change; viral loads in the lungs, nasal passages, and brain; and histological examination of the lungs at day 4 post-challenge. Safety criteria included evaluation of pathogenicity and transmissibility in hamsters and ts phenotype stability during prolonged in vitro cultivation. Results: The F-F3 strain displayed a stable ts phenotype in vitro, did not infect hamster lungs or brain, and showed no transmission from immunized to naïve co-housed animals. A single intranasal immunization by F-F3 induced seroconversion, reduced pneumonia severity by 76.2% and 79.5% in two independent experiments (p < 0.01), protected the lungs against productive infection while reducing viral load in the nasal passages, and resulted in no detectable viral transmission after homologous BA.5.2 challenge. Following heterologous Wuhan-like challenge, immunization prevented weight loss and significantly reduced viral loads in the lungs, nasal passages, and brain; however, protection against pneumonia was only modest (18.6%; p < 0.05). Conclusions: Preclinical evaluation of the F-F3-based LAV prototype demonstrated a favorable balance between safety and efficacy. These characteristics support its further consideration as a candidate strain for COVID-19 LAV development.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of an intranasal live attenuated vaccine (LAV) candidate based on a temperature-sensitive (ts) Omicron-like SARS-CoV-2 mutant in a Syrian hamster model. The F-F3 strain was characterized using electron microscopy, nanopore sequencing, cytopathic effect titration, and RT-PCR. In vitro studies were conducted on Vero CCL-81 cells, while in vivo studies assessed transmissibility and efficacy in female hamsters. The study is limited to animal models and lacks human trials, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has ended, emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants remain a future threat.
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of an intranasal live attenuated vaccine (LAV) prototype based on a temperature-sensitive (ts) Omicron-like SARS-CoV-2 mutant in a Syrian hamster COVID-19 model.
elements_zh.methods: 通过电子显微镜、纳米孔测序、细胞病变效应滴定和 RT-PCR 对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Dubrovka(武汉样)、Otradnoe(BA.1.1)和 FEB2(BA.5.2)菌株以及源自 FEB2 的 ts F-F3 突变体进行了表征。体外研究使用 Vero CCL-81 细胞;在雌性叙利亚仓鼠中评估了体内传播性和功效研究。通过ELISA和中和测定来测量血清抗体滴度。通过体重变化评估免疫效果;肺部、鼻道和大脑中的病毒载量;攻击后第 4 天进行肺部组织学检查。
elements_zh.main_results: F-F3菌株在体外表现出稳定的ts表型,不感染仓鼠肺或脑,并且未表现出来自免疫至首次共养动物的传播。F-F3 的单次鼻内免疫诱导了血清转化,在两个独立实验中将肺炎严重程度降低了 76.2% 和 79.5% (p < 0.01),保护肺部免受生产性感染,同时减少了鼻道中的病毒载量,并且在同源 BA.5.2 攻击后没有检测到病毒 传播。在经历类似武汉的异源攻击后,免疫接种阻止了体重减轻,并显着减少了肺部、鼻道和大脑中的病毒载量;然而,对肺炎的保护作用不大(18.6%;p < 0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: Preclinical evaluation of the F-F3-based LAV prototype demonstrated a favorable balance between safety and efficacy. These characteristics support its further consideration as a candidate strain for COVID-19 LAV development.
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于 F-F3 的 LAV 可能是在新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体背景下进一步开发的有希望的候选者,特别是其安全性和针对同源挑战的功效。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于叙利亚仓鼠模型的临床前评估,该模型可能无法完全代表人类 免疫应答。证据是温和的,因为它是基于体外和体内研究而没有进行人体试验。

papers.title: Association of In-Hospital Antimalarial–Macrolide Therapy With 3–6-Month Cardiac Electrophysiological Outcomes in Survivors of Severe COVID-19: A Matched Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: During the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic, antimalarial agents and macrolide antibiotics were widely used because of their proposed antiviral and immunomodulatory effects. However, their potential to prolong ventricular repolarization and increase the risk of arrhythmias raised concerns about their cardiac electrophysiological effects. Available evidence has predominantly focused on electrophysiological effects during acute treatment, whereas post-recovery outcomes remain less well characterized. Objectives: To evaluate cardiac electrophysiological outcomes 3–6 months after hospitalization for severe COVID-19 pneumonia and compare these outcomes according to in-hospital exposure to combined antimalarial–macrolide therapy. Methods: We conducted a retrospective matched cohort study including adults hospitalized for severe COVID-19 pneumonia between March and June 2020. Patients exposed to hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine in combination with azithromycin or clarithromycin were matched 1:1 by sex and age (±3 years) with patients who did not receive either drug class. Cardiovascular assessment 3–6 months after hospitalization included a 12-lead electrocardiogram and 24-hour Holter monitoring. QTc interval, conduction abnormalities, arrhythmias, and heart rate variability (HRV) were evaluated. Results: Eighty-six patients were included (43 exposed and 43 unexposed). Follow-up QTc intervals were similar between groups (420.0 vs. 423.1 ms; p =0.762), and QTc prolongation was uncommon. No malignant ventricular arrhythmias or clinically significant conduction abnormalities were identified. Exposed patients had a higher prevalence of sinus bradycardia, a lower resting heart rate on electrocardiography, and higher HRV as assessed by the standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN). However, unexposed patients exhibited a greater inflammatory burden during hospitalization, more frequent intensive care unit admissions, and longer hospital stays. Conclusion: In this cohort of survivors of severe COVID-19, short-term in-hospital exposure to combined antimalarial–macrolide therapy was not associated with persistent QTc prolongation or clinically significant electrophysiological abnormalities at 3–6 months. Differences in heart rate and HRV should be interpreted with caution, given potential residual confounding due to acute disease severity.

papers.title: The role of VWF/ADAMTS13 axis in COVID-19-associated coagulopathy
papers.abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019, which broke out in 2019, is a disease caused by SARS-CoV-2 infection. Although this infection mainly affects the respiratory system, a high incidence of thrombotic events has been observed in severe or critically ill cases and in a considerable number of non-survivors of COVID-19. Although the coagulation dysfunction and hypercoagulability of COVID-19 have been reported in the literature, the specific situation of its coagulation function has not been fully studied. The observation of microvascular thrombosis in COVID-19 patients has attracted our attention to investigate the potential inflammatory endothelial injury or damage. Von Willebrand factor (VWF) and its proteolytic protease, A D isintegrin A nd M etalloproteinase with T hrombo S pondin type 1 motifs, 13 (ADAMTS13), play an important role in maintaining the vascular health and organ perfusion. Therapeutic and prophylactic anticoagulation are important measures to prevent these kinds of thrombotic events, but new treatments such as recombinant ADAMTS13 and anti-VWF nanobody Caplacizumab are being studied in vitro for thrombosis with high efficacy. This review focuses on the discussion of the current research progress of the treatment of COVID-19-associated coagulopathy by correcting the imbalance of VWF-ADAMTS13 axis, the existing problems, and the prospects.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review investigates the role of the VWF/ADAMTS13 axis in the coagulopathy associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, focusing on its impact on thrombotic events in severe or critically ill cases and non-survivors of COVID-19.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative analysis of existing literature on the VWF/ADAMTS13 axis and its involvement in coagulopathy in SARS-CoV-2 infection. It does not report specific databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that while coagulation dysfunction and hypercoagulability in COVID-19 have been reported, the specific mechanisms involving the VWF/ADAMTS13 axis remain underexplored. It emphasizes the importance of this axis in maintaining vascular health and organ perfusion.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the specific situation of coagulation function in SARS-CoV-2 infection has not been fully studied, indicating a gap in understanding the precise role of the VWF/ADAMTS13 axis in thrombotic events. It also mentions the need for further research on new treatments like recombinant ADAMTS13 and anti-VWF nanobody Caplacizumab.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on clarifying the role of the VWF/ADAMTS13 axis in SARS-CoV-2-associated coagulopathy and exploring the efficacy of novel treatments such as recombinant ADAMTS13 and Caplacizumab in preventing thrombotic events.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of the VWF/ADAMTS13 axis in the coagulopathy associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly in severe or critically ill cases and non-survivors of COVID-19. It highlights the importance of this axis in maintaining vascular health and organ perfusion, while noting that the specific mechanisms of coagulation dysfunction in SARS-CoV-2 remain underexplored. The review underscores the need for further research to understand the precise role of the VWF/ADAMTS13 axis and to evaluate the potential of new treatments like recombinant ADAMTS13 and Caplacizumab in preventing thrombotic events. These findings suggest that targeted studies on the VWF/ADAMTS13 axis could lead to improved therapeutic strategies for managing coagulopathy in SARS-CoV-2 infections.

papers.title: From past to present and toward the future: a mechanism-informed clinical framework for COVID-19-associated headache and post-viral pain
papers.abstract: Headache is a prominent acute and persistent neurological manifestation of COVID-19, representing both as a significant clinical challenge and a valuable model for understanding the neurotropic effects of SARS-CoV-2. This review synthesizes evidence showing that the epidemiology of COVID-19 headache is distinctly shaped by younger age, female sex, and a prior history of headache disorders; its clinical phenotypes are diverse, strongly associating with chemosensory dysfunctions such as anosmia; and its core pathophysiology involves neuroinflammation (e.g., cytokine-mediated pathways), trigeminovascular activation, and sex-specific neuroendocrine-immune interactions. Although acute headache often responds to conventional analgesics, persistent cases—a major component of Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC)—necessitate a multidisciplinary management approach. This contrasts with the typically self-limiting headache following vaccination. Future research should prioritize longitudinal studies to define chronicity, mechanistic investigations into sex-specific pathways, and the development of phenotype-specific, personalized therapeutic strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review article explores the clinical and pathophysiological aspects of headache associated with COVID-19, emphasizing its role as a significant neurological manifestation of SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study highlights that headache is more prevalent in younger individuals, females, and those with a history of headache disorders, and is strongly linked to chemosensory dysfunctions like anosmia. The core mechanisms involve neuroinflammation, trigeminovascular activation, and sex-specific neuroendocrine-immune interactions. While acute headaches may respond to standard analgesics, persistent cases, particularly those linked to Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), require a multidisciplinary approach. The article notes that headache following vaccination is typically self-limiting, contrasting with the chronic nature of post-COVID headaches. It concludes by advocating for future research to focus on longitudinal studies, sex-specific mechanisms, and personalized therapeutic strategies for managing persistent post-COVID headaches.

papers.title: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Cancer patients face a significantly elevated risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes. Although vaccination is a cornerstone of prevention, data on vaccination coverage and association with survival among Russian cancer patients remain scarce. We assessed COVID-19 vaccination coverage and its association with overall survival in a population-based cohort of cancer patients in Northwest Russia. Methods This retrospective registry-based cohort study integrated data from the Population-Based Cancer Registry (PBCR) of the Arkhangelsk Region and the Nenets Autonomous Okrug, regional vaccination records, and an artificial intelligence (AI)-based analysis of chest computed tomography (CT) scans. The cohort consisted of 1,144 cancer patients who underwent CT between August 2020 and April 2021. Vaccination status was ascertained via data linkage. Overall survival (OS) was compared between vaccinated and unvaccinated patients using Kaplan–Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for demographic, clinical, and AI-derived CT biomarkers. To mitigate immortal time bias, the primary analysis used a landmark approach restricted to patients alive on March 1, 2021 (N = 1,136). A sensitivity analysis used a November 1, 2021 landmark (N = 894). Vaccination status was defined as receipt of at least one dose before the landmark date. Results Only 6.6% (n=76) of patients received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine (Sputnik V or Sputnik Light). Vaccinated patients were more likely to have earlier-stage cancer and were less likely to be receiving active treatment. In the primary landmark analysis, vaccination was associated with a significantly higher 3-year OS (80.3% vs. In multivariable analysis, vaccination was independently associated with a 60% lower hazard of all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.25–0.64). AI-detected COVID-19 pneumonia on baseline CT was also an independent predictor of poorer survival (adjusted HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.09–1.59). In the sensitivity analysis (November 1, 2021 landmark), the adjusted HR for vaccination was 0.56 (95% CI 0.34–0.92), showing a consistent but attenuated association. Conclusion This study reveals critically low COVID-19 vaccination coverage among cancer patients in Northwest Russia. Nevertheless, vaccination was strongly associated with a substantial survival benefit, underscoring its importance as a potentially lifesaving intervention for this vulnerable population.

papers.title_zh: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Cancer patients face a significantly elevated risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes. Although vaccination is a cornerstone of prevention, data on vaccination coverage and association with survival among Russian cancer patients remain scarce. We assessed COVID-19 vaccination coverage and its association with overall survival in a population-based cohort of cancer patients in Northwest Russia. Methods This retrospective registry-based cohort study integrated data from the Population-Based Cancer Registry (PBCR) of the Arkhangelsk Region and the Nenets Autonomous Okrug, regional vaccination records, and an artificial intelligence (AI)-based analysis of chest computed tomography (CT) scans. The cohort consisted of 1,144 cancer patients who underwent CT between August 2020 and April 2021. Vaccination status was ascertained via data linkage. Overall survival (OS) was compared between vaccinated and unvaccinated patients using Kaplan–Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for demographic, clinical, and AI-derived CT biomarkers. To mitigate immortal time bias, the primary analysis used a landmark approach restricted to patients alive on March 1, 2021 (N = 1,136). A sensitivity analysis used a November 1, 2021 landmark (N = 894). Vaccination status was defined as receipt of at least one dose before the landmark date. Results Only 6.6% (n=76) of patients received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine (Sputnik V or Sputnik Light). Vaccinated patients were more likely to have earlier-stage cancer and were less likely to be receiving active treatment. In the primary landmark analysis, vaccination was associated with a significantly higher 3-year OS (80.3% vs. In multivariable analysis, vaccination was independently associated with a 60% lower hazard of all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.25–0.64). AI-detected COVID-19 pneumonia on baseline CT was also an independent predictor of poorer survival (adjusted HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.09–1.59). In the sensitivity analysis (November 1, 2021 landmark), the adjusted HR for vaccination was 0.56 (95% CI 0.34–0.92), showing a consistent but attenuated association. Conclusion This study reveals critically low COVID-19 vaccination coverage among cancer patients in Northwest Russia. Nevertheless, vaccination was strongly associated with a substantial survival benefit, underscoring its importance as a potentially lifesaving intervention for this vulnerable population.

papers.title: Biological and societal impacts of combination antiviral therapy for SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern
papers.abstract: The development of vaccines targeting SARS-CoV-2 has been heavily studied since the start of COVID-19 and its declaration by WHO as a pandemic in March of 2020. However, with the emerging variants of concern (VoCs), such as Omicron and Delta, research into antiviral therapy in addition to vaccines is essential to help combat current and future VoCs. Recent studies have shown that multidrug therapy combining a variety of antivirals targeting different aspects of the SARS-CoV-2 lifecycle could be more effective at suppressing the virus, and could potentially reduce the risk of developing viral resistance. However, with these benefits also come concerns surrounding the feasibility and safety of administering a combination of drugs. This article will discuss the current state of knowledge pertaining to combination antiviral therapy against SARS-CoV-2 to determine the benefits and disadvantages from a health and molecular biology perspective. Additionally, this article will be looking into the societal perceptions and ramifications of antivirals against SARS-CoV-2, and whether there is less hesitancy in taking antivirals as compared to getting vaccinated. With 2 million unvaccinated young children in Canada, as well as patients suffering with various immunological disorders, it is even more important to explore different options of protection against SARS-CoV-2 for those who are unable to get vaccinated. When designing these therapies, it will be essential to consider the social accessibility of the drug in addition to its biological effectiveness. In an increasingly globalized world, interdisciplinary work will be critical to having a more complete understanding of an area of research, particularly in the field of health and medicine. By exploring the two topics above, this article will aim to unite the social and biological perspectives on combination antiviral therapy in relation to the COVID-19 pandemic.

papers.title_zh: 抗病毒药物 组合疗法对相关 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异的生物学和社会影响
papers.source_body_en: The development of vaccines targeting SARS-CoV-2 has been heavily studied since the start of COVID-19 and its declaration by WHO as a pandemic in March of 2020. However, with the emerging variants of concern (VoCs), such as Omicron and Delta, research into antiviral therapy in addition to vaccines is essential to help combat current and future VoCs. Recent studies have shown that multidrug therapy combining a variety of antivirals targeting different aspects of the SARS-CoV-2 lifecycle could be more effective at suppressing the virus, and could potentially reduce the risk of developing viral resistance. However, with these benefits also come concerns surrounding the feasibility and safety of administering a combination of drugs. This article will discuss the current state of knowledge pertaining to combination antiviral therapy against SARS-CoV-2 to determine the benefits and disadvantages from a health and molecular biology perspective. Additionally, this article will be looking into the societal perceptions and ramifications of antivirals against SARS-CoV-2, and whether there is less hesitancy in taking antivirals as compared to getting vaccinated. With 2 million unvaccinated young children in Canada, as well as patients suffering with various immunological disorders, it is even more important to explore different options of protection against SARS-CoV-2 for those who are unable to get vaccinated. When designing these therapies, it will be essential to consider the social accessibility of the drug in addition to its biological effectiveness. In an increasingly globalized world, interdisciplinary work will be critical to having a more complete understanding of an area of research, particularly in the field of health and medicine. By exploring the two topics above, this article will aim to unite the social and biological perspectives on combination antiviral therapy in relation to the COVID-19 pandemic.

papers.title: Municipality-level ecological analysis of COVID-19 mortality and infections in Austria, 2020 to 2023
papers.abstract: Background: Previous studies indicated that regional fluctuations in COVID-19 impact were associated with socioeconomic, demographic and environmental factors early in the pandemic. It is unclear whether factors associated with regional COVID-19 mortality and SARS-CoV-2 infections changed over the course of the pandemic. Methods: We evaluated the association of ecological factors with municipality-specific COVID-19 mortality in the national population of Austria between January 2020 and June 2023. Analyses were conducted separately per calendar year and pooled across years via random-effects meta-analysis. Outcomes were analysed using univariable and multivariable zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression, including annually averaged environmental exposome exposure (including air pollution and UV radiation), socioeconomic, demographic and infection dissemination predictors with significance threshold set to p<0.005. Secondary analysis modelled SARS-CoV-2 infections using of negative-binomial model (NB). Two additional approaches for smaller predictor set selection were applied as sensitivity analyses. Results: Within the entire observation period 18,430 COVID-19 deaths were reported. In univariable analyses (pooled RR (99.5% CI)), COVID-19 mortality was significantly associated with the proportion of commuters (0.79 (0.73-0.86)), residents aged 75-84 (1.18 (1.01-1.37)) and [≥]85 years (1.29 (1.04-1.60)), residents with at most compulsory education (1.15 (1.02-1.29)), employed residents aged 15-64 (0.89 (0.85-0.93)), and homeowners (0.91 (0.83-0.99)), as well as with precipitation (0.94 (0.89-0.99)) and the average time with a mean temperature of 5-15 C (0.95 (0.90-0.99)). In multivariable analyses the share of population aged 85 or older (1.30 (1.09-1.54)) and home ownership (0.92 (0.87-0.98)) were independently significant. Mortality predictor estimates were relatively stable across pandemic years. Across 5,963,882 documented SARS-CoV-2 infections share of employed in 15- to 64-year-olds (1.01 (1.01-1.02)), part-time employment rate (1.01 (1.00-1.02)) and district level nursing care allowance recipiency (0.97 (0.95-0.98)) were associated with detected infections. Overnight stays, population 85 or older, income, compulsory education or less and air pollution all had multiple significant estimates with opposite directionality, leading to non-significant overall associations. Sensitivity analyses outcomes mirrored main analyses outcomes. Conclusions: Throughout the pandemic in Austria, demographic and socioeconomic factors were associated with COVID-19 mortality and infections, but many associations, especially for infections, were unstable over time. These findings underscore the importance of structural vulnerabilities in epidemic impact.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted an ecological analysis of SARS-CoV-2 mortality and infections at the municipality level in Austria from 2020 to 2023. It aimed to assess whether factors influencing regional impacts of the pandemic changed over time. The study used zero-inflated negative binomial regression and random-effects meta-analysis to evaluate associations between ecological factors, socioeconomic variables, and demographic characteristics with mortality and infections. Results showed that factors such as age distribution, employment status, and housing conditions were significantly associated with mortality, while some variables, like air pollution and overnight stays, had mixed effects. The study's ecological design limits the strength of its conclusions, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the nature of the associations observed.
